requirement: Coverage is validated independently of an available test framework

files.note: The GUT reference test, exercised for the reference artifact only.

No GUT dependency despite living under tests/ -- placed there specifically so gd-tools' own default test_dirs exclusion (['test', 'tests']) keeps it out of the coverage plan itself, exactly like F004's excluded test file.

inputs.name: default
inputs.call: check.py -> real gd-tools test --coverage (reference), then a from-scratch manual driver with no GUT/gd-tools CLI, both calling subject.gd:run(3) then run(0) (gd-tools-cli 0.4.0)

measured_with_gd_tools_0_4_0.finding: A manual driver -- no GUT, no gd-tools CLI, just the raw `_GDTCoverage` autoload plus ~15 lines of hand-written glue -- produces coverage data EXACTLY equal to the real GUT-path artifact for an identical execution. This is possible because gd-tools' actual GUT integration (pre_run_hook.gd, post_run_hook.gd) is itself only thin glue over a runner-agnostic autoload: pre_run_hook.gd's entire job is one line (`_GDTCoverage.set_active(true)`), and post_run_hook.gd's entire job is reading `get_hits()` and writing JSON. Neither does anything GUT-specific to the tracking mechanism itself.

notes: Confirms the requirement by EQUALITY against a real GUT-path artifact, not merely 'the manual driver produced some plausible-looking hits' -- equality is what actually proves framework independence, since a merely-plausible result could still hide a subtle instrumentation difference. One real timing bug was found and fixed while building this fixture: `_GDTCoverage`'s own `_ready()` (where instrumentation via `Script.reload(true)` actually happens) fires on the autoload's first idle frame, the same as any other node's `_ready()` -- NOT synchronously before a SceneTree script's `_initialize()` runs. Calling `set_active(true)` and the subject directly from `_initialize()` sees the ORIGINAL, uninstrumented source and silently collects zero hits (confirmed empirically: an early draft produced `{}`). The fix is `call_deferred()` to let that first frame turn before doing anything -- documented in manual_driver.gd's own comment, since this is exactly the kind of gap a real standalone integration would need to know about and this fixture makes it an explicit, checked fact rather than a footnote.
